lessons.claim: ★ Rolling resistance is **exactly equivalent** to a harmonic bending stiffness -- kappa_theta_eff = (1/2)*k_roll*R^2 (in the limit where the orientational degree of freedom relaxes). The derivation: U_r = k_r R^2 (2 - (a_i - a_j).n_hat) (a = a body-fixed contact-point marker), and minimizing over the orientation theta gives theta_k=(phi_{k-1}+phi_k)/2 for an internal particle while an end particle relaxes fully to theta=phi, leaving U_r = (1/4) k_r R^2 * sum(theta_bend^2) -- the internal particles being shared between both bonds and thereby frustrated is the origin of the bending stiffness. Measured (the 3-point bending stiffness, an analytic-gradient scipy minimization, n=3/5/9/15): rolling/harmonic = 1.00000/0.99999928/0.99999085/0.99999475. Raising delta by 100x leaves k_roll unchanged at 1.000003x (a genuine quadratic stiffness).
